passage: The evening bus from the plains had already gone when Anirban closed the shutter of the tea stall in the hill town, and Dolma was waiting on the bench outside. A month ago Anirban had found the messages. Dolma had lied within their marriage, and there was nothing to argue about. Tonight there were questions. Where, how long, who else knew. Dolma answered each one plainly, even when the answer was ugly, without adding "but". When Anirban's voice cracked with anger, Dolma stayed on the bench and did not look away. At the end Dolma said, "I'm not asking you to forgive me quickly. I'll answer anything, any time." Anirban walked up the lane ahead, then slowed once to let Dolma catch up, and did not say anything.

qa.q: Where was Dolma waiting when Anirban closed the stall?
qa.a: On the bench outside the tea stall.

qa.q: What does Dolma want, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Dolma seems remorseful and wants the marriage to survive: Dolma stays, answers every question plainly and says, "I'm not asking you to forgive me quickly."

qa.q: Why did Dolma avoid adding "but" to the answers?
qa.a: Adding "but" would have turned honest answers into excuses and defence. Answering plainly lets Anirban see the whole truth and set the pace of trust.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Dolma's behaviour tonight?
qa.a: Anirban may feel angry and hurt but also notice the honesty, since Anirban slowed once to let Dolma catch up, though the silence shows nothing is settled.

grounding: Shows a partner who broke trust and wants the marriage to survive, accepting anger, answering questions honestly without defensiveness and letting trust return at the other's pace.

passage:
The waiting room at the family counselling centre had one fan and a poster about healthy communication. Gargi sat on one plastic chair and Aparna sat three chairs away. It had been two months since Aparna found out about Gargi's affair with a woman from her running club.

In the session Aparna asked, again, "How many times did you meet her?" Gargi had answered it four times already. She felt the old urge: I've told you. Why do you keep asking?

She didn't say it. "Eleven times. Mostly after running. Twice at her flat."

Aparna's face hardened. "I hate you right now."

Gargi's throat ached. "That's fair. I did that to us."

The counsellor asked Gargi what she wanted from Aparna. Gargi said, "Nothing I can ask for. I want to earn it back, at whatever speed she needs." Aparna didn't look at her. But she didn't leave either.

qa.q: How many times did Gargi say she met the woman?
What was Gargi feeling when Aparna asked the question again?
qa.a: Gargi felt the urge to be defensive and impatient, and also a painful ache of guilt.

qa.q: How did Gargi handle Aparna's anger and questions?
qa.a: Gargi answered honestly again, accepted Aparna's anger without defending, and said she would earn trust at Aparna's pace.

qa.q: How does Aparna feel during the session?
qa.a: Aparna feels intense anger and hurt, saying she hates Gargi, but staying in the room suggests she hasn't fully given up.

grounding: The counselling scene shows a young wife who broke her partner's trust accepting anger, answering questions honestly and letting trust return at the partner's pace.

passage:
Dhruv,

I'm writing because when I try to say this out loud, I cry, and then you end up comforting me, and that's backwards.

I broke your trust. For four months I lied to you about Kunal. I'm not going to explain it away.

I know you're angry. You have every right to be. When you shout, I'm going to listen, not defend. When you ask me the same question for the tenth time, I'll answer it the tenth time, honestly. My phone is on the table whenever you want it.

I want our marriage to survive. But I also know that asking you to forgive me quickly would be another way of putting myself first. So I won't ask. You set the pace. If it takes years, it takes years.

If, after all that, you decide you can't, I'll have to accept it.

Damini

qa.q: How long did Damini lie to Dhruv?
What does Damini feel when trying to talk about it out loud?
qa.a: Damini feels overwhelmed with guilt and cries, which ends with Dhruv doing the comforting.

qa.q: What promises does Damini make to help rebuild trust?
qa.a: Damini promises to listen instead of defending, answer every question honestly, keep the phone open and let Dhruv set the pace.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel reading that Damini won't ask for quick forgiveness?
qa.a: Dhruv may still feel angry and hurt, but perhaps also a little safer, since the pace is now Dhruv's.

grounding: The letter shows a young spouse who broke a partner's trust accepting the partner's anger, answering honestly and letting trust return at the partner's pace rather than asking for quick forgiveness.
